conviction_note: Three of the four things ABM's whole fiscal-2026 guide depends on got measurably better in third-party data published AFTER management last spoke on 2026-06-05 (record US storage installs plus a raised 2026 storage forecast, the best US office absorption quarter in seven years, and the Q2 10-Q footnote confirming the prior-year self-insurance actuarial review is done and produced no charge), against one that got worse (airline clients' cost shock deepened in July); netting them and then haircutting hard for the genuinely demanding H2 EPS arithmetic that IS in the wire gets me to about +1.5 points, well inside the 6.67% median reaction because ABM's Q3 prints are historically its quietest (+0.33% on 2025-09-05 even while walking guidance to the low end).

findings.finding: US energy storage installed a record 20.2 GWh in calendar Q2 2026 (17.9-18.0 GWh utility-scale, 1.8 GWh commercial/industrial), 30.8 GWh in H1, and SEIA/Benchmark RAISED the full-year 2026 forecast to 71 GWh versus 59 GWh installed in 2025 - published 2026-09-01, twelve weeks after ABM last spoke, and covering the two months (May, June) that sit inside ABM's fiscal Q3.
findings.why_not_priced: ABM's Technical Solutions grew 27.2% in Q2 FY26 explicitly on battery energy storage, and the entire FY26 adjusted-EPS guide rests on management's claim that 'volume will ramp meaningfully in ATS' in the back half - the single most doubted line in the guide, because ATS margin was diluted in Q2 by equipment-heavy BESS work. The datapoint that validates it sits in solar/storage trade press a week before the print, on a $2.8bn company with only three published estimates; no ABM preview carries it. If the market had made the connection, ABM would not be sitting 4.68% below its 52-week high with 15.1% annualised realised vol into a print where its fastest-growing segment's end market just set an all-time quarterly record and had its annual outlook raised 20%. Note this also refutes the Wood Mackenzie call (published 2025-07-01) that US grid-scale BESS would contract 29% in 2026 on FEOC and tariff constraints, which is the version of this story that was current when ABM guided.
findings.independence: Independently reported the same day by a different trade outlet from the same SEIA/Benchmark release: https://www.solarpowerworldonline.com/2026/09/q2-was-biggest-quarter-ever-for-energy-storage-installs-in-the-us/ (2026-09-01). Directionally corroborated by a separate, unrelated demand channel - hyperscaler capex guidance was raised again at the late-July/early-August 2026 prints (Amazon to ~$220bn from ~$200bn, Alphabet to $195-205bn from $180-190bn) per https://www.tmtfinance.com/intel/2026-hyperscaler-capex-tops-us700bn-analysis - which feeds the same ATS data-centre electrical book. Shares no document with any other finding in this file.

findings.finding: CBRE's Q2 2026 US office report (2026-07-29) shows national vacancy falling 30bp to 18.3% - 'the largest quarterly decline since 2015' - net absorption of 12.6m sq ft, nearly double the prior quarter and a ninth straight positive quarter, leasing +16% y/y, with CBRE projecting 2026 annual leasing to surpass the 2022 record; San Francisco, the exact market ABM's CEO singled out on 2026-06-05 as having vacancy 'probably 2 or 3x worse than New York City', posted +963,980 sq ft of net absorption in the quarter.
findings.why_not_priced: Business & Industry is ~44% of ABM revenue ($1,015.8m of $2,290.0m in Q2) and was flat y/y, which management attributed to UK and West Coast client exits driven by CRE weakness. The office inflection is fully priced in office REITs, which are the constituency that reads CBRE Figures; it is not priced in a janitorial contractor covered by three analysts, because the transmission runs through re-scoping, occupancy-linked hours and win rates rather than through any line an ABM preview models. If it were priced you would see ABM bid into the print rather than -3.07% over 20 days, and you would see at least one of the three estimates moving after 2026-07-29. Sized small deliberately: janitorial scope lags leasing by several quarters, and near-term reported B&I is dominated by the disclosed Transport for London exit worth ~300bp of back-half B&I growth, so this is a tone-and-FY27 item more than a Q3 revenue item.
findings.independence: A different firm, different methodology, same direction and published separately: Colliers' Q2 2026 US office statistics report the strongest quarterly net absorption in seven years with national vacancy at ~18% - https://www.colliers.com/en/research/nrep-usofc-us-office-market-statistics-2026-q2. San Francisco detail is a second CBRE document (https://www.cbre.com/insights/figures/san-francisco-office-figures-q2-2026, 2026-07-10), so treat the two CBRE files as one source cluster with Colliers as the genuinely independent leg.

findings.finding: ABM Aviation grew 19.5% in Q2 and its CEO warned on 2026-06-05 that 'rising fuel costs will likely create some near-term challenges for our airline clients'; since then the airline cost shock deepened rather than resolved - American Airlines cut FY26 guidance a second time in July (to a -$0.65 to +$0.65 adjusted EPS range from -$0.40 to +$1.10, with a Q3 loss guide, on ~$3.75/gal fuel), Southwest cut FY26 to $3.25-$4.25 from 'at least $4' after a ~$900m y/y Q2 fuel increase, and Alaska has had guidance suspended since April.
findings.why_not_priced: Aviation is 13.5% of ABM revenue ($310.8m, $16.3m segment operating profit in Q2) and was the second-fastest-growing segment, and the market is extrapolating the Heathrow ramp. Airline distress is completely priced in airline equities - it is not priced in a name screened as defensive facility services, and none of the three published ABM estimates models an airline procurement squeeze on outsourced cabin, ground and passenger-assistance scope. If the market had priced it, ABM's 25-delta skew would be visibly bid for downside and the stock would be more than 4.68% off its high with realised vol above 15%. Sized small on purpose and honestly: TSA throughput set records through June and July 2026 so in-quarter volumes were fine, the direct Q3 EPS arithmetic of even a 5% Aviation revenue shortfall is roughly a penny, most ABM airline contracts pass through labour, and the industry capacity trim was already partly visible before ABM guided on 2026-06-05. The risk here is to forward commentary and FY27 framing, not to the Q3 number.
findings.independence: Partial only. BofA's carrier-capacity tracking (Q3 2026 domestic growth cut to ~0.8%, American to 7.5% from 9.3%, Delta to 1.2%) points the same way - https://m.investing.com/news/analyst-ratings/bofa-cuts-airline-capacity-outlook-as-carriers-trim-september-plans-93CH-4710071 - but that page carries a corrupt primary timestamp and a 2026-05-26 update stamp, i.e. it may pre-date ABM's guide, so I am not resting the finding on it. The ABM-side leg is management's own 2026-06-05 remark in the transcript: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/06/08/abm-abm-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/

findings.finding: Note 8 of the Q2 FY26 10-Q states that ABM performed its review of the majority of its casualty insurance programmes during Q2 2026 and 'it was determined that there was no adjustment required for our total reserves related to prior years during the six months ended April 30, 2026' - so the item that produced a $(22.2)m pre-tax hit (~100bp of adjusted EBITDA margin, ~$0.26/sh) in Q4 FY25 is a Q2/Q4 event and is very unlikely to appear in the Q3 print, even though ABM's adjusted EPS definition now includes it while its guidance range is stated 'before any impact from prior-year self-insurance adjustments'.
findings.why_not_priced: ABM changed its non-GAAP definition after SEC staff comment (disclosed 2025-12-17) so that reported adjusted EPS now INCLUDES prior-year self-insurance adjustments, while the $3.85-$4.15 guide explicitly excludes them. That mismatch is the mechanical reason FY25 landed at $3.44 against a $3.65-$3.80 range, and it is the most plausible single source of a headline 'miss' on this name. Three analysts on a $2.8bn company are not reading Note 8 of a June 10-Q to work out the actuarial cadence, and there is no aggregator field for 'timing of casualty reserve reviews'. If the market had priced the absence of this risk you would not see an indicative 8.13% implied move on a 93-contract chain with a 1.32 put/call OI ratio. This is a left-tail-removal finding, not a mean finding, which is why it is sized at less than half a point.
findings.independence: The $(22.2)m Q4 FY25 magnitude and the non-GAAP definition change come from a different document - the FY25 results release, https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/12/17/3206839/799/en/ABM-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Fiscal-2025-Results-and-Provides-Fiscal-2026-Outlook.html (2025-12-17). No other finding in this file rests on the 10-Q, so there is no source-cluster overlap.

searched_and_found_nothing: EDGAR full filing list: nothing filed since 2026-07-17 (last Form 4) and no 8-K since 2026-06-05 - no quiet 8-K, no August insider activity, no acquisition, no credit-agreement amendment ahead of the print

ABM's own newsroom June-September 2026: only a LaGuardia Terminal B autonomous-robotics pilot (2026-07-28), an Atlanta Braves/Truist Park venues agreement (2026-06-16) and a sales-award PR - no material contract win or loss announced in the quarter
CEO/CFO succession or executive departures - nothing since the January 2026 CIO/CSO promotions

Activist or strategic-alternatives angle: JCP Investment Management showed a ~$6.2m ABM position in Q2 2026 13Fs, which is ~0.2% of the market cap and not a campaign; the two April 2026 Schedule 13Gs are passive (one is Vanguard Capital Management LLC)
ICE/I-9 worksite enforcement against ABM specifically - the sector-level risk is real and rising but no ABM-specific audit, raid, notice of inspection or fine is findable

Semiconductor fab construction as a WGNSTAR risk: the US fab delays that are findable (Intel Ohio to 2030, Micron Clay NY to 2030) were announced in Feb 2025 and Nov 2025 respectively, i.e. long before ABM guided, so they are not new information into this print

BLS Employment Cost Index for Q2 2026 (private wages decelerating to 3.1% from 3.4%, real wages -0.4%) - a genuine labour-cost tailwind for the most labour-intensive name in the group, but macro, widely published on 2026-07-31 and not ABM-specific enough to carry as a finding

Segment backlog: ABM discloses no segment backlog; the only quantified figure in the Q2 10-Q is $222.3m of remaining performance obligations, which excludes variable consideration and series contracts and is therefore not comparable to the Comfort Systems / EMCOR backlog figures the sweep suggested cross-checking

ERP / internal-control angle: the ERP transition survives only as a forward-looking-statement risk factor; the working-capital reset already happened and is visible in a +$179m six-month operating cash-flow swing reported on 2026-06-05, so it is priced
careers.abm.com does not resolve, so no job-postings-by-title count was obtainable
No ABM app-store, status-page, changelog or customer-forum surface exists to read - it is a B2B labour services company
baseline_tension: It cuts against the run-in: the baseline shows a stock drifting -3.07% over 20 days and -4.68% off its high with a 1.32 put/call OI ratio, while the post-guide third-party data on the two end markets the FY26 guide actually depends on (utility-scale/C&I storage and US office demand) both improved and the 10-Q footnote says the recurring self-insurance charge is off the table for Q3 - the only thing agreeing with the soft tape is the airline cost shock, which is the smallest of the four and the one whose EPS arithmetic is a penny.
